transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, hi. So, I guess I'm here because... well, my wife and my supervisor at the plant, they both keep getting on my case about the exact same thing. They keep saying I’m not listening to them. Like, my supervisor will be standing right in front of me, talking straight to my face. We run these heavy stamp presses on the production floor, right? And the noise in there is just unbelievable. You gotta wear the foam plugs plus the heavy earmuffs if you don't want to go deaf, which, honestly, my uncle went deaf in one ear from working construction because he never wore protection back in the day... but anyway, Dave—my supervisor—will be talking to me, and a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what he said. 

Same thing with my wife at home. I'll be looking right at her, but then I have to ask her to say it all over again. Which really ticks Dave off at work because he's already stressed about the supply chain issues we're having with the aluminum sheets, you know? It's been an absolute nightmare getting materials in on time since last month, the trucks are always late. But yeah, that's what brought me in. I just keep missing what people are saying when they talk to me.
Do you notice this trouble hearing equally in both ears, or is one ear worse than the other?

Oh, no, it's not—my hearing itself is fine. Both ears are exactly the same. We actually have to do those mandatory hearing tests every year at the plant. OSHA rules, you know? They put you in this tiny little soundproof booth, looks almost like an old phone booth from the nineties. Remember those? Man, you just don't see payphones anywhere anymore. I actually saw one at a gas station out on Route 9 last week and the receiver was completely ripped off the cord. Just dangling there. Who even does that? 

But anyway, the booth... they play these tiny little beeps and you press a button. My hearing is perfect on paper. The company nurse, Brenda, she said my chart is totally fine. Brenda's been there for like thirty years, she's retiring next month actually. We're doing a big potluck for her on the Friday shift, I'm supposed to bring potato salad. But yeah, physically, my ears work fine. Both of them. It's not a hearing thing, it's just... the words don't stick in my head, I guess.
Aside from missing spoken words, do you also notice yourself losing focus or making careless mistakes during other tasks that don't involve listening, like reading a report or doing paperwork?

Yeah, it's not just the listening stuff. Like, on the line, we have these quality checks we gotta do before the parts go out. I just sort of rush through them, honestly. I'll end up missing these little things, like a wrong label on the box or a loose fitting somewhere. Which is crazy because the new labels they just started using are this bright, neon yellow. They switched from the white ones last month because the old barcode scanners were having trouble reading them under the fluorescent lights. Man, those lights give me a headache by the end of the shift. They just buzz constantly. 

But yeah, I'll miss a loose fitting or put the wrong label on, and then Dave has to pull me aside again because it just keeps happening. He usually takes me into the breakroom to talk about it, and it's right next to this vending machine that has been broken for like three weeks. It ate my dollar on Tuesday when I just wanted a pack of peanuts. I told maintenance about it, but they're always backed up fixing the forklifts. The transmission on forklift number three is completely shot, it just grinds when you put it in reverse. But anyway, yeah, Dave gets pretty mad because I keep rushing and messing up those little details on the checks.

Thinking back to your school years or childhood, did you have similar trouble paying attention, staying focused, or following instructions back then, or is this something that's only started more recently as an adult?

Yeah, no, it's always been like this. Even back when I was a kid. I remember in elementary school, the teachers were constantly moving my desk around. Like, they'd put me right up front by the chalkboard, then they'd move me to the back corner because I just couldn't stay put in my chair. Those old wooden desks with the metal legs, you know? The ones where the chair is attached to the desk part. They always squeaked so loud if you shifted around. My buddy Mike had one that wobbled, and he used to stick folded up pieces of paper under the leg to balance it. Mike actually works at the plant with me now, down in shipping. Small world, right? We used to ride bikes everywhere when we were kids. He had this sweet red Schwinn with the banana seat. 

But yeah, in school, I was always getting in trouble. I'd just blurt out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. Or I'd get up and start messing with what the other kids were doing. I just couldn't help it, I'd butt right into their projects or whatever. It was really bad before middle school. I spent a lot of time in the principal's office. Mr. Henderson. He had this giant jar of jellybeans on his desk, but he never actually gave them out to anybody. Just sat there, collecting dust. I always wondered if they were even real or just plastic decorations. But yeah, it's definitely not a new thing, I've always been this way.
